Text2What you need to know about your Xbox 360 console.
<font size="16" color= "#FFFFFF" >Press the Xbox Guide button to get to almost everything on your console.

<font size="16" color= "#FFFFFF" > Your Xbox 360 console provides robust parental control features.
To set up, go to System Settings, Family Settings.
<font size="16" color= "#FFFFFF" > Edit your profile and select Privacy Settings to limit who can contact you and what you see online.
You can also mute individual players, provide feedback, or file a complaint from the player's profile.
Text3Catch the most exciting features on Xbox 360 today.
<font size="16" color= "#FFFFFF" >Make your profile a little more personal with your own avatar. Dress yourself up, or go a little wild!</font>

Now you can browse, download and play full Xbox 360 games without leaving the couch.  Plus, you can redownload purchased games at any time on Xbox LIVE.
<font size="16" color= "#FFFFFF">Xbox LIVE is the free online service for Xbox 360.  Download and play games, watch movies* and enjoy free game trials.
<font size="16" color= "#FFFFFF">If you are upgrading to a new console or storage device, you can transfer your content right from the Xbox Dashboard.

Xbox LIVE members may want to add your child to their friends list. You can require these requests to be approved by you, or allow your child to approve them on their own.
Require Approval: Require that all new friend requests be approved by you. You'll also need to approve any new friend requests that your child wants to send to other people.
Approval Not Required: Let your child send and accept new friend requests on their own.
Friends lists connect you with people you like to play with. When an Xbox LIVE member adds someone to their friends list, that person receives a friend request, which they can accept or reject.

Use New Online Friends in Family Settings to keep your child from sending or accepting friend requests without your permission. To approve friend requests, you'll need to enter your Windows Live ID password.
Some Family Settings have a Friends Only option. If you use this option to approve friend requests, your child will be able to interact only with people you approve.

This test detects your network adapter and verifies that it is physically connected.  If you are using a wired-only connection, this test verifies that an Ethernet cable is connected to your console's Ethernet port.  If you are using an Ethernet-to-wireless bridge, this test verifies that your console can communicate with your wireless bridge.  If you are using the Xbox 360 Wireless Networking Adapter, this test verifies that your adapter is properly connected to your console.
Note: The Xbox 360 Wireless Network Adapter is disabled while an Ethernet cable is plugged into your console's Ethernet port.

If you've tried these suggestions and your console still does not pass this test, go to www.xbox.com/setup or call Xbox Customer Support.
This test verifies that the wireless adapter connected to your console is connected to a wireless network.  If your console does not pass this test:
If you are using an Xbox 360 Wireless Networking Adapter, verify that an Ethernet cable is NOT plugged into your console's Ethernet port.
Remove any obstructions between your Xbox 360 console and your wireless access point.
Turn off any devices that may interfere with your wireless network (for example, microwave ovens or 2.4-GHz telephones).

If you are using an infrastructure network, make sure the security settings on your wireless adapter match those on your wireless access point, gateway, or router (for example, your WEP key or WPA passphrase must match).
If you are establishing an ad-hoc network, make sure the network name, channel, band and security settings match the settings on the device you are establishing a connection with.
If you've tried these suggestions and your console still does not pass this test, go to www.xbox.com/setup or call Xbox Customer Support.
Confirm that there are no other devices on your network with the same IP address.
If you are using a router or gateway, verify that it is configured to assign IP addresses to network devices (DHCP enabled).

If you are connecting directly to a modem and have replaced a device that was connected to your modem with your console or another device, turn the modem off and back on before connecting the new device.

If your console is connected to an ad-hoc network, it will probably not pass this test. If your IP address is assigned automatically and your ad-hoc network does not include a DHCP server, this does not indicate a problem. The test is properly reporting that a DHCP server could not be contacted.
If you've tried these suggestions and your console still does not pass this test, go to www.xbox.com/setup or call Xbox Customer Support.
If you've tried these suggestions and your console still does not pass this test, go to www.xbox.com/setup or call Xbox Customer Support.

This test confirms that your network has a sufficient Maximum Transmission Unit (MTU). MTU is a setting on your router or gateway that can affect network performance. Xbox Live requires a minimum MTU setting of 1364. If your console does not pass this test, you will not be able to sign in to Xbox Live. See your router or gateway instruction manual for information about changing the MTU setting.
If you change your MTU setting and your console still does not pass this test, go to www.xbox.com/setup or call Xbox Customer Support.

This test evaluates how your router or gateway will respond to a particular type of Internet Control Message Protocol (ICMP) packet. If your network fails this test, you will not be able to sign in to Xbox Live. To fix, remove the router or gateway from your network or replace it with an Xbox Live Compatible router or gateway. For a listing of devices that have earned this certification, go to www.xbox.com.
If you've tried this suggestion and your console still does not pass this test, go to www.xbox.com/setup or call Xbox Customer Support.

This test verifies that your console can contact Xbox Live. If your console does not pass this test, check your IP Confirmed, DNS Verified, MTU, and ICMP tests. A failure on any of these tests will prevent you from signing in to Xbox Live. If your console passes all of these tests and still cannot sign in to Xbox Live, verify that your account information is accurate and up to date.
If you've tried these suggestions and your console still does not pass this test, go to www.xbox.com/setup or call Xbox Customer Support.

This test indicates the type of Network Address Translation (NAT) that your router or gateway is using. Devices that perform strict or moderate NAT can limit the ability of gamers to find each other, participate in sessions, or hear each other on Xbox Live.

You will not receive a result for this test if you are unable to sign in to Xbox Live. If you do not receive a result, test your connection to Xbox Live. If your router or gateway is using a moderate or strict NAT, replace it with an Xbox Live Compatible device. For a listing of devices that have earned this certification, see www.xbox.com.
If you've tried these suggestions and your console still does not pass this test, go to www.xbox.com/setup or call Xbox Customer Support.
